### https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals_television_ratings
# NBA Finals television ratings

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a list of [television ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_ratings "Nielsen ratings") for [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), based on [Nielsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research") viewing data.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)

The highest rated and most watched NBA Finals series was the [1998 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_NBA_Finals "1998 NBA Finals") between the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997-98_Chicago_Bulls_season "1997-98 Chicago Bulls season") and [Utah Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997–98_Utah_Jazz_season "1997–98 Utah Jazz season"), which averaged an 18.7 rating / 33 share and 29.04 million viewers on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_on_NBC "NBA on NBC"). That series also featured the highest rated and most watched NBA Finals game, as the Sunday night averaged a 22.3 rating / 38 share and 35.89 million viewers. The [1987 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_NBA_Finals "1987 NBA Finals") between the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986–87_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "1986–87 Los Angeles Lakers season") and [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986–87_Boston_Celtics_season "1986–87 Boston Celtics season") was the highest rated and most watched NBA Finals series on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_on_CBS "NBA on CBS"), averaging a 15.9 rating / 32 share and 24.12 million viewers. Game 7 of the [1988 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_NBA_Finals "1988 NBA Finals") registered the network's highest rated and most watched NBA game with a 21.2 rating / 37 share.

The [2015 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_Finals "2015 NBA Finals") between the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014–15_Golden_State_Warriors_season "2014–15 Golden State Warriors season") and [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014–15_Cleveland_Cavaliers_season "2014–15 Cleveland Cavaliers season") was the highest rated NBA Finals series on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_on_ABC "NBA on ABC") averaging an 11.6 rating / 21 share and 19.94 million viewers. The [2026 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_Finals "2026 NBA Finals") between [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025–26_New_York_Knicks_season "2025–26 New York Knicks season") and [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025–26_San_Antonio_Spurs_season "2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season") was the most watched NBA Final series on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_on_ABC "NBA on ABC") averaging a 9.4 rating / 31 share and 20.58 million viewers. Game 7 of the [2016 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_Finals "2016 NBA Finals") registered the network's highest rated and most watched NBA game with an average 15.8 rating / 29 share and 31.02 million viewers.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) It was the first [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") game to draw more than 30 million average viewers in 18 years, and only the seventh non-[NFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") sports telecast (excluding the [Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games")) to have done so since 1998.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Game7Rating-3)

The [2019 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NBA_Finals "2019 NBA Finals") between the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018–19_Golden_State_Warriors_season "2018–19 Golden State Warriors season") and the [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018–19_Toronto_Raptors_season "2018–19 Toronto Raptors season") had a drop in American viewership however combined North American viewership. Analysts cited the presence of a Canadian team (Canadian viewership does not count towards U.S. Nielsen ratings, leading to only one U.S. home market being reflected in viewership), as a factor in the drop.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) At the same time, the presence of the Toronto Raptors in the NBA Finals boosted Canadian viewership to record levels.[\[6\]](#cite_note-ca_g1_ratings-6)

For the [2020 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_Finals "2020 NBA Finals"), the ratings dropped to a historic low, with one of the games drawing only 5.1 million viewers.[\[7\]](#cite_note-yahoo_20202-7) The average viewers figure over 6 games was 7.5 million, which is a 51% decline from the previous year.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) Some have claimed this was due to the players' political activism; others have claimed this was due to the finals being played out of season caused by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), as other sports such as the [NHL playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL_playoffs "NHL playoffs") and the [MLB playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_playoffs "MLB playoffs") also showed a significant decline in ratings.[\[7\]](#cite_note-yahoo_20202-7)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The 2026 Knicks-Spurs Finals set record viewership since 1998. According to ESPN, Game 5 of the 2026 Finals peaked at 33 million viewers as Jalen Brunson led a fourth-quarter comeback (https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49086824/knicks-title-clinching-win-vs-spurs-most-watched-nba-finals-game-5-1998) — this is an instantaneous peak-concurrent-audience figure, not a cumulative reach number. Dividing 33 million by the 2026 U.S. population (~345-348 million) yields roughly 9.5%, matching Rovell's figure, though no source explicitly states '9.5%' — this is an inferred calculation from the raw peak-viewer number, not something stated in any article.

For 1998, Wikipedia's page on the 1998 NBA playoffs explicitly states that Game 6 'was the highest rated and most watched game in NBA History, with 72 million viewers watching at least part of the game and an average of 35.9 million viewers in the U.S.' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_NBA_playoffs). The 72 million figure is explicitly a cumulative 'watched at least part of the game' reach statistic, fundamentally different from an instantaneous peak-audience measurement. Dividing 72 million by the 1998 U.S. population (~270-276 million) yields approximately 26%, matching Rovell's '26.1 percent,' though again no source explicitly calculates or states this percentage — it is an inferred calculation, not a sourced claim.

The core issue: Rovell compares a true instantaneous peak-audience percentage for 2026 (~9.5%, from the 33 million peak concurrent viewership) against a cumulative total-reach percentage for 1998 (~26.1%, from the 72 million who watched 'all or part' of the broadcast per Wikipedia's 1998 NBA playoffs page). These are different metrics that are not directly comparable — a cumulative 'watched any part' figure will always be substantially larger than an instantaneous peak-moment figure, since it aggregates all unique viewers who tuned in at any point during a multi-hour broadcast. This mismatch makes the 1998 audience appear to dwarf the 2026 audience 'at its height' by a much larger margin than a true apples-to-apples comparison would show. A fair comparison would use peak-to-peak or cumulative-to-cumulative figures for both years; for reference, Front Office Sports notes 1998's Game 6 'remains the most watched NBA game in history, totalling 35.9 million viewers' as its average (not peak) audience (https://frontofficesports.com/most-watched-nba-finals/), which would be a more appropriate benchmark against the 2026 Game 5's 24.5 million average (https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49086824/knicks-title-clinching-win-vs-spurs-most-watched-nba-finals-game-5-1998).

# Knicks-Spurs most-watched NBA Finals since 1998; averaged 20.6M - ESPN

play

*   ESPN News Services
    

Jun 16, 2026, 06:26 PM ET

NEW YORK -- The [New York Knicks](/nba/team/_/name/ny/new-york-knicks)' [94-90 victory](/nba/game/_/gameId/401859967/knicks-spurs) over the [San Antonio Spurs](/nba/team/_/name/sa/san-antonio-spurs) on Saturday night to [capture their first NBA title in 53 years](/nba/story/_/id/49056351/knicks-rally-again-vs-spurs-capture-first-nba-title-1973) averaged 24.5 million viewers on ABC and ESPN, making it the most-watched Game 5 since 1998.

The audience peaked at 33 million, as Finals MVP [Jalen Brunson](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3934672/jalen-brunson) was putting the wraps on a 45-point performance as the Knicks rallied from a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter.

Overall, the Finals averaged 20.6 million, according to Nielsen, the highest since the 1998 series between [Chicago](/nba/team/_/name/chi/chicago-bulls) and [Utah](/nba/team/_/name/utah/utah-jazz) when Michael Jordan won his sixth and final NBA title (averaged 29.04 million in six games).

This year's ratings were also the highest since ABC and ESPN started carrying the NBA Finals in 2003.

It is only the third time since 1999 that the Finals have averaged at least 20 million.

[Golden State](/nba/team/_/name/gs/golden-state-warriors)'s victory over [Cleveland](/nba/team/_/name/cle/cleveland-cavaliers) in five games in 2017 averaged 20.47 million, while the 2016 Finals, where the Cavaliers defeated the Warriors in seven games, averaged 20.2 million.

Last year's Finals between [Oklahoma City](/nba/team/_/name/okc/oklahoma-city-thunder) and [Indiana](/nba/team/_/name/ind/indiana-pacers) averaged 10.31 million across seven games.

FINAL IS TOP-RATED PRO HOOP GAME EVER

June 16, 1998 More than**28 years ago**

By David Bauder

NEW YORK, JUNE 16 -- The Chicago Bulls victory that clinched the NBA championship was the highest-rated pro basketball game ever broadcast.

Sunday's sixth and final game in the series with the Utah Jazz had a 22.3 rating and 38 percent audience share, with NBC estimating today that 72 million people watched all or part of it. The previous top-rated NBA broadcast was the seventh game of the Finals between the Detroit Pistons and Los Angeles Lakers in 1988.

## Research findings (background — not a source)
Rovell's framing conflates two different audience metrics for the two eras, making the comparison misleading. For the 2026 Knicks-Spurs Finals, the 9.5% figure appears to correspond to the game's peak concurrent audience: Game 5 'peaked at 33 million viewers' (https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49086824/knicks-title-clinching-win-vs-spurs-most-watched-nba-finals-game-5-1998), which is about 9.7% of the roughly 340 million U.S. population in 2026 - a genuine 'at its height' instantaneous peak audience figure. For the 1998 Bulls-Jazz Game 6, however, the 26.1% figure does not match the actual peak Nielsen rating. According to Nielsen data, Game 6 'had a 22.3 rating and 38 percent audience share, with NBC estimating today that 72 million people watched all or part of it' (https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1998/06/17/bulls-a-winner-for-nbc/9e4ac4dd-ecb0-4aa8-b6fd-a6f6e56535a6/). The 72 million figure is a cumulative 'watched all or part' reach number - not a simultaneous peak audience - and 72 million divided by the roughly 270-276 million U.S. population in 1998 yields approximately 26%, matching Rovell's '26.1 percent' claim. Wikipedia's NBA Finals ratings page shows Game 6 averaged a 22.3 rating and 35.89 million viewers (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals_television_ratings), figures well below the 72 million cumulative reach number used in the post. So the post compares a true instantaneous peak audience percentage (2026, ~9.5%) against a cumulative/total-reach percentage (1998, ~26.1%), which are not equivalent measurements. This apples-to-oranges comparison overstates how much larger the 1998 audience was 'at its height' relative to 2026, since the 2026 number reflects a true peak-moment statistic while the 1998 number reflects total unique viewers over the whole broadcast.

The **1998 NBA playoffs** was the postseason tournament of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association")'s [1997–98 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997–98_NBA_season "1997–98 NBA season"). The tournament concluded with the two-time defending NBA champion and [Eastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Conference_\(NBA\) "Eastern Conference (NBA)") champion [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls") defeating the [Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_\(NBA\) "Western Conference (NBA)") champion [Utah Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Jazz "Utah Jazz") 4 games to 2 in the [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_NBA_Finals "1998 NBA Finals"). The Bulls achieved a second three peat, a goal unrivaled since the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") in [1966](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_NBA_playoffs "1966 NBA playoffs"). Michael Jordan was named [NBA Finals MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award") for the sixth and final time.

The [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets "Brooklyn Nets") made the playoffs for the first time since [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993–94_New_Jersey_Nets_season "1993–94 New Jersey Nets season"), but did not appear again until [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_NBA_playoffs "2002 NBA playoffs"). Their presence was a mere asterisk compared to what they accomplished in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001–02_New_Jersey_Nets_season "2001–02 New Jersey Nets season"), getting swept by the eventual champion Bulls.

The Minnesota Timberwolves won their first playoff game in franchise history by winning Game 2 of their series against the Seattle SuperSonics. However, the SuperSonics prevailed in five games despite the Timberwolves taking a 2–1 series lead.

The [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") lost to Indiana in the first round 3–1 and did not appear again until [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005–06_Cleveland_Cavaliers_season "2005–06 Cleveland Cavaliers season"). It would also be the final playoff appearance for the Cavaliers without [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") on the roster.

The Heat–Knicks series was extremely notable for two reasons

*   Game 4: A fight broke out between [Larry Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Johnson_\(basketball,_born_1969\) "Larry Johnson (basketball, born 1969)") and [Alonzo Mourning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alonzo_Mourning "Alonzo Mourning") at the end of the game (in which the Knicks won 90–85). A lasting image of the fight was Knicks coach [Jeff Van Gundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Van_Gundy "Jeff Van Gundy") clinging to Mourning's leg. Both players were suspended for two games. Johnson and Mourning had bad blood dating back to their stint as [Charlotte Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Hornets "Charlotte Hornets") teammates.
*   Game 5: The New York Knicks became the fourth seventh seed to knock off a second seeded team in the first round of the playoffs. This would not occur again until [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_playoffs "2010 NBA playoffs").

Game 5 of the Jazz–Rockets series would be the final game of [Clyde Drexler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Drexler "Clyde Drexler")'s career.

The [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997–98_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "1997–98 Los Angeles Lakers season") advanced to the Western Conference Finals for the first time since [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990–91_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "1990–91 Los Angeles Lakers season"). They were ultimately swept by the Jazz.

The [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997–98_Indiana_Pacers_season "1997–98 Indiana Pacers season") entered the postseason with a franchise record 58 wins. Although they would lose to the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997–98_Chicago_Bulls_season "1997–98 Chicago Bulls season") in the Eastern Conference Finals, this team was later named by Pacers.com as the greatest in franchise history primarily due to their record, even better than the [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999–2000_Indiana_Pacers_season "1999–2000 Indiana Pacers season") team that won the Eastern Conference Title. The Eastern Conference Finals series between the Chicago Bulls and Indiana Pacers was extremely notable for several reasons:

*   Game 4: [Reggie Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Miller "Reggie Miller")'s game winning 3 pointer with 0.7 seconds, which has been marked one of the greatest postseason moments in NBA History. Michael Jordan attempted a game winning 3 pointer of his own, but it rimmed out, effectively tying the series at 2–2.
*   Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Finals: With a win, the Pacers took the Bulls to the limit by becoming 1 of only 2 teams to force a Game 7 in the Bulls' title years (the [Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991–92_New_York_Knicks_season "1991–92 New York Knicks season") achieved this in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_NBA_playoffs "1992 NBA playoffs")).
*   Game 7: This was the first (and as of 2025, only) Game 7 to take place at the [United Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Center "United Center").[](https://www.nba.com/pacers/running-at-the-bulls-oral-history-1997-98-pacers-pt-2)
*   Game 7: This was the last Game 7 the Bulls would play until [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NBA_playoffs "2009 NBA playoffs").

For the first time since [1989 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_NBA_Finals "1989 NBA Finals"), there was a rematch of the same two teams: the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997–98_Chicago_Bulls_season "1997–98 Chicago Bulls season") and the [Utah Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997–98_Utah_Jazz_season "1997–98 Utah Jazz season"). This would not happen again until [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_Finals "2014 NBA Finals").

[Game 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_6_of_the_1998_NBA_Finals "Game 6 of the 1998 NBA Finals") of the NBA Finals was extremely notable for several reasons:

*   In the waning moments of the game [Michael Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") made the title winning shot over [Bryon Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryon_Russell "Bryon Russell"). This moment was marked as one of the greatest moments in NBA playoff history.
*   It was the highest rated and most watched game in NBA History, with 72 million viewers watching at least part of the game and an average of 35.9 million viewers in the U.S.
*   It was the last Chicago Bulls postseason game until [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_NBA_playoffs "2005 NBA playoffs") and the last involving the Michael Jordan-led Bulls.
*   Michael Jordan's final NBA playoff game.
*   [Phil Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Jackson "Phil Jackson")'s final game as coach of the Chicago Bulls (he would go on to coach the Los Angeles Lakers two seasons later).
*   As of 2026, this remains the most recent NBA Finals game for the Chicago Bulls and the Utah Jazz.

# Knicks-Spurs most-watched NBA Finals since 1998; averaged 20.6M - ESPN

play

Stephen A. apologizes to Jalen Brunson for doubting him (2:07)

*   ESPN News Services
    

Jun 16, 2026, 06:26 PM ET

NEW YORK -- The [New York Knicks](/nba/team/_/name/ny/new-york-knicks)' [94-90 victory](/nba/game/_/gameId/401859967/knicks-spurs) over the [San Antonio Spurs](/nba/team/_/name/sa/san-antonio-spurs) on Saturday night to [capture their first NBA title in 53 years](/nba/story/_/id/49056351/knicks-rally-again-vs-spurs-capture-first-nba-title-1973) averaged 24.5 million viewers on ABC and ESPN, making it the most-watched Game 5 since 1998.

The audience peaked at 33 million, as Finals MVP [Jalen Brunson](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3934672/jalen-brunson) was putting the wraps on a 45-point performance as the Knicks rallied from a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter.

Overall, the Finals averaged 20.6 million, according to Nielsen, the highest since the 1998 series between [Chicago](/nba/team/_/name/chi/chicago-bulls) and [Utah](/nba/team/_/name/utah/utah-jazz) when Michael Jordan won his sixth and final NBA title (averaged 29.04 million in six games).

This year's ratings were also the highest since ABC and ESPN started carrying the NBA Finals in 2003.

It is only the third time since 1999 that the Finals have averaged at least 20 million.

[Golden State](/nba/team/_/name/gs/golden-state-warriors)'s victory over [Cleveland](/nba/team/_/name/cle/cleveland-cavaliers) in five games in 2017 averaged 20.47 million, while the 2016 Finals, where the Cavaliers defeated the Warriors in seven games, averaged 20.2 million.

Last year's Finals between [Oklahoma City](/nba/team/_/name/okc/oklahoma-city-thunder) and [Indiana](/nba/team/_/name/ind/indiana-pacers) averaged 10.31 million across seven games.

_The Associated Press contributed to this report._

The 2026 Knicks-Spurs Finals set record viewership since 1998. According to ESPN, Game 5 of the 2026 Finals peaked at 33 million viewers as Jalen Brunson led a fourth-quarter comeback (https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49086824/knicks-title-clinching-win-vs-spurs-most-watched-nba-finals-game-5-1998) — this is an instantaneous peak-concurrent-audience figure, not a cumulative reach number. Dividing 33 million by the 2026 U.S. population (~345-348 million) yields roughly 9.5%, matching Rovell's figure, though no source explicitly states '9.5%' — this is an inferred calculation from the raw peak-viewer number, not something stated in any article.

For 1998, Wikipedia's page on the 1998 NBA playoffs explicitly states that Game 6 'was the highest rated and most watched game in NBA History, with 72 million viewers watching at least part of the game and an average of 35.9 million viewers in the U.S.' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_NBA_playoffs). The 72 million figure is explicitly a cumulative 'watched at least part of the game' reach statistic, fundamentally different from an instantaneous peak-audience measurement. Dividing 72 million by the 1998 U.S. population (~270-276 million) yields approximately 26%, matching Rovell's '26.1 percent,' though again no source explicitly calculates or states this percentage — it is an inferred calculation, not a sourced claim.

The core issue: Rovell compares a true instantaneous peak-audience percentage for 2026 (~9.5%, from the 33 million peak concurrent viewership) against a cumulative total-reach percentage for 1998 (~26.1%, from the 72 million who watched 'all or part' of the broadcast per Wikipedia's 1998 NBA playoffs page). These are different metrics that are not directly comparable — a cumulative 'watched any part' figure will always be substantially larger than an instantaneous peak-moment figure, since it aggregates all unique viewers who tuned in at any point during a multi-hour broadcast. This mismatch makes the 1998 audience appear to dwarf the 2026 audience 'at its height' by a much larger margin than a true apples-to-apples comparison would show. A fair comparison would use peak-to-peak or cumulative-to-cumulative figures for both years; for reference, Front Office Sports notes 1998's Game 6 'remains the most watched NBA game in history, totalling 35.9 million viewers' as its average (not peak) audience (https://frontofficesports.com/most-watched-nba-finals/), which would be a more appropriate benchmark against the 2026 Game 5's 24.5 million average (https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49086824/knicks-title-clinching-win-vs-spurs-most-watched-nba-finals-game-5-1998).

first.findings: Post claims Penny from Big Bang Theory "was a prostitute... implied in the show" and befriended the guys because they were furthest from clients. Canon contradicts this: Penny Hofstadter is established as an aspiring, mostly unsuccessful actress born on a farm near Omaha, Nebraska, who worked at The Cheesecake Factory as a waitress until she quit in "The Occupation Recalibration" (S7E13) to act full-time, later becoming a pharmaceutical rep in season 8 https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Penny_Hofstadter . Pilot canon has her describing her screenplay about a girl from Lincoln, Nebraska who comes to LA to be an actress and ends up a waitress at the cheesecake factory, clarifying "No, I'm from Omaha!" https://the-big-bang-theory.com/quotes/character/Penny/ (pilot quote). No episode, writer or producer source lists sex work as her job; promiscuity is a running slut-shaming joke, but analysis notes she had roughly five confirmed partners vs Raj's at least 10 https://screenrant.com/big-bang-theory-penny-raj-sleep-together/ , undermining conflation of dating jokes with prostitution. The only "prostitute" lines are jokes: e.g. Penny in "The Financial Permeability" asks "That I'm some sort of Chinese food prostitute?" https://the-big-bang-theory.com/quotes/quote/941/ , and season 2 episode "The Vegas Renormalization" features a separate prostitute character Mikayla, not Penny. Darker original unaired pilot female lead Katie (Amanda Walsh) was described as darker/street-hardened and taking advantage of Sheldon/Leonard, but she was scrapped and replaced by Penny https://www.thethings.com/the-big-bang-theory-chuck-lorre-leonard-sheldon-roommate-katie-penny-kaley-cuoco/  — not canon evidence Penny was a prostitute.
first.note: Penny is established in canon as an aspiring actress from Omaha who worked as a waitress at The Cheesecake Factory until season 7. No episode or producer source identifies her as a sex worker; the "prostitute" line is a joke about Chinese food, not her job.

## Penny Hofstadter

  
**Penelope "Penny" Hofstadter** is the show _The Big Bang Theory_'s first and always main female protagonist. She lives in [Apartment 4B](/wiki/Apartment_4B "Apartment 4B") with her husband Leonard Hofstadter across the hall from Sheldon Cooper, who lives in apartment 4A where Leonard used to live with Sheldon as roommates. Although the sleeping arrangements are a little complicated. This was an accommodation for Sheldon who was having a very hard time dealing with his break-up with Amy, and Leonard moving out in The 2003 Approximation. Leonard also maintains an office in 4A. Her full first name is possibly "Penelope" as implied by "[The Barbarian Sublimation](/wiki/The_Barbarian_Sublimation "The Barbarian Sublimation")", and her maiden name has never been revealed. But due to her recent marriage to Leonard, her last name is Hofstadter. For a while her last name was Johnson while unknowingly married to ex-boyfriend Zack Johnson. That marriage was annulled in [The Thanksgiving Decoupling](/wiki/The_Thanksgiving_Decoupling "The Thanksgiving Decoupling").

An aspiring, but mostly unsuccessful actress, she was born on a farm near Omaha, Nebraska, and worked at The Cheesecake Factory as a waitress until she quit in "[The Occupation Recalibration](/wiki/The_Occupation_Recalibration "The Occupation Recalibration")" (S7E13) to take up acting full time. Penny is the original female lead in the show before being joined by [Bernadette Rostenkowski](/wiki/Bernadette_Rostenkowski-Wolowitz "Bernadette Rostenkowski-Wolowitz") and [Amy Farrah Fowler](/wiki/Amy_Farrah_Fowler "Amy Farrah Fowler") in seasons 3 and 4, and in season 8, started working at the same company as Bernadette.

Since the pilot, she has always been Leonard's love interest, with the two dating briefly in the first episode of the second season, for most of the third season, and they rekindled their romance in "The Recombination Hypothesis". As of "[The Gorilla Dissolution](/wiki/The_Gorilla_Dissolution "The Gorilla Dissolution")", she and Leonard became engaged and were married at the start of season 9 in The Matrimonial Momentum.

Even though she is considered part of the guys' group, she represents the "dumb blonde" for viewer context in the series with many street smarts and communication skills to compensate for her lack of academic knowledge.

## Physical Appearance\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny is a slender, young woman with fair skin, blond hair and wears different types of clothing, mainly tank tops and jeans.

When she first moved into apartment 4B, she wore a light blue t-shirt, jean short shorts and brown boots.

## Personality\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny is somewhat naive and not thoroughly educated but has a lot of common sense and street smarts. Her dream is to become a famous actress, a goal she never seems to waver from until season 8. She is very kind-hearted and empathetic toward people though she can blow up when made mad, which prompted Leonard to refer to her as The Incredible Hulk" after she went off on Howard. She believes most guys are nice and has been hurt a lot. When someone shocks her, she tends to bat her eyes at them while considering her response. She also walks away when frustrated with people like Sheldon or situations she can't believe or understand. She knows how to throw out wise-cracks and is very loyal to her man as long as she is not betrayed. She also tends to deny doing embarrassing things, or she suddenly realizes they are embarrassing. In the first season, she seemed very naive but has appeared smarter in later seasons and more complicated in situations with her female friends. She also has a habit of being selfish and throwing her friends under the bus. For example, she sold Sheldon out to the court officials for running a red light, despite the fact he had done it to help her after she had dislocated her shoulder, simply because she didn't want the ticket.

### Season 1\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

[![Penny blackmails Sheldon](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/warner-bros-entertainment/images/2/21/Bbt-sheldon-penny.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20220512040537)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/warner-bros-entertainment/images/2/21/Bbt-sheldon-penny.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220512040537)

[](/wiki/File:Bbt-sheldon-penny.jpg)

Penny blackmails Sheldon

In the [first episode](/wiki/Pilot "Pilot") Penny moves into Apartment 4B across from Apartment 4A where Leonard and Sheldon live. She had broken up with her boyfriend Kurt because he cheated on her. She asked the guys for a favor to go get her TV from his apartment, but he steals their pants and Penny apologizes for everything and later the three go out to dinner with Howard and Raj.

In "[The Big Bran Hypothesis](/wiki/The_Big_Bran_Hypothesis "The Big Bran Hypothesis")", Penny asks Leonard and Sheldon to sign for her delivery of her entertainment center. When Sheldon and Leonard, they discover that Penny's apartment is a mess, prompting Sheldon to try to clean it. When Penny arrives, they leave. Unbeknown to her at night, Sheldon cleans up the apartment anyway. When Penny wakes up the next morning, she is infuriated that Sheldon and Leonard came into her apartment while she was asleep, and forces Leonard to give back her spare keys. Sheldon forcefully apologizes to Penny and reveals that he cleaned her apartment. Penny bumps into Raj and she explains the situation, although Raj can't speak to her, he is a good listener, Penny decides to forgive Leonard, and when Leonard tries to apologize, she immediately forgives him.

### Season 2\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D5&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

[![Sheldon helping Penny get an enchanted sword](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/warner-bros-entertainment/images/4/4e/2x03-The-Barbarian-Sublimation-penny-and-sheldon-22774835-1580-888.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20220512040725)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/warner-bros-entertainment/images/4/4e/2x03-The-Barbarian-Sublimation-penny-and-sheldon-22774835-1580-888.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220512040725)

[](/wiki/File:2x03-The-Barbarian-Sublimation-penny-and-sheldon-22774835-1580-888.jpg)

Sheldon helping Penny get an enchanted sword

After a post-date disagreement, Penny remains friends with all four guys, becomes an integral part of the Social Group and very good friends with Leonard.

In "[The Hofstadter Isotope](/wiki/The_Hofstadter_Isotope "The Hofstadter Isotope")", Penny is asked out on a date by Stuart and things end later in the next episode after it is revealed she called Stuart "Leonard".

In the season finale "[The Monopolar Expedition](/wiki/The_Monopolar_Expedition "The Monopolar Expedition")", Penny wishes Leonard wasn't going to the North Pole and even gives Leonard a blanket as a good luck gift on his expedition to the North Pole.

### Season 3\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D6&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

When the guys return from the North Pole, Penny has missed Leonard enough to express her feelings for him, and they date for most of the season.

Penny introduces her friend Bernadette to Howard as part of a Girlfriend Pact made between Howard and Leonard. Things don't go too smoothly until the two of them find out they both have overbearing mothers.

### Season 4\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D7&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny resumes being part of the guys group and has her own friends, Bernadette, along with Sheldon’s new girlfriend, [Amy](/wiki/Amy_Farrah_Fowler "Amy Farrah Fowler"). Also she realizes that she still has feelings for Leonard, especially since Leonard is dating Priya.

### Season 5\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D8&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Half way through the season (on the 100th episode), Leonard asks Penny out and they reunite, though Penny has misgivings.

### Season 6\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D9&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny works through her doubts and has a stronger relationship with Leonard, as she is now able to say "I love you" to him. They discuss marriage.

### Season 7\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D10&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny finds out she is legally married to Zack after Leonard, Sheldon and Amy tell her that weddings in Las Vegas wedding chapels are real when the two thought they were fake. At the end, she and Zack fill out annulment papers and the marriage is legally annulled ("[The Thanksgiving Decoupling](/wiki/The_Thanksgiving_Decoupling "The Thanksgiving Decoupling")"). Penny quits The Cheesecake Factory to concentrate on acting ("[The Occupation Recalibration](/wiki/The_Occupation_Recalibration "The Occupation Recalibration")") and becomes engaged to Leonard after she gets over her clash with the director who fired her ("[The Gorilla Dissolution](/wiki/The_Gorilla_Dissolution "The Gorilla Dissolution")").

### Season 8\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D11&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Between the finale of Season 7 and the premiere of Season 8, Penny drastically changes her look by swapping her usual long blonde locks for a short blonde pixie crop, a look she sports throughout the entire season. She gets a new job at Bernadette's company as a pharmaceutical rep, making excellent progress in her field and spending the year as Leonard's fiancée. At the end of the season, she suggests they head to Vegas to get married.

### Season 9\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D12&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Leonard's little make-out session at sea makes their marriage have a rocky start, but they quickly reconcile though they don't move out of Sheldon's apartment (because of Sheldon going through a bad breakup and due to Sheldon's abandonment issues). At the end of the season, when it's revealed that everyone is upset about not being part of the wedding due to their elopement, Penny suggests having a redo wedding ceremony.

### Season 10\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D13&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

In "The Conjugal Conjecture" Penny and Leonard have their re-wedding ceremony in a park which is officiated by Bernadette.

Penny and Leonard finally have their own apartment, Apartment 4A. In "[The Cohabitation Experimentation](/wiki/The_Cohabitation_Experimentation "The Cohabitation Experimentation")", Amy's apartment suffered water damage, was uninhabitable and she needed a place to stay. Sheldon and Amy started a five week experiment to see if they could manage living together and moved into Penny's old apartment, Apartment 4B. It turned into a permanent arrangement in "[The Veracity Elasticity](/wiki/The_Veracity_Elasticity "The Veracity Elasticity")". Penny also redecorates her and Leonard's bedroom.

### Season 11\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D14&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

While Sheldon proposes to Amy, he gets a call from Leonard and Penny, asking about where he is. He tells them about his unwilling kiss with Ramona and how it made him realize his true feelings about Amy. At the same time, Bernadette tells Penny that she’s pregnant again.

### Season 12\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D15&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Sheldon and Amy win the Nobel prize with Penny, Leonard, Howard, Bernadette and Raj coming to watch his speech. He then tells the story of his family who has changed his life. Penny And Leonard are soon to be parents.

## Research findings (background — not a source)
Post claims Penny from Big Bang Theory "was a prostitute... implied in the show" and befriended the guys because they were furthest from clients. Canon contradicts this: Penny Hofstadter is established as an aspiring, mostly unsuccessful actress born on a farm near Omaha, Nebraska, who worked at The Cheesecake Factory as a waitress until she quit in "The Occupation Recalibration" (S7E13) to act full-time, later becoming a pharmaceutical rep in season 8 https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Penny_Hofstadter . Pilot canon has her describing her screenplay about a girl from Lincoln, Nebraska who comes to LA to be an actress and ends up a waitress at the cheesecake factory, clarifying "No, I'm from Omaha!" https://the-big-bang-theory.com/quotes/character/Penny/ (pilot quote). No episode, writer or producer source lists sex work as her job; promiscuity is a running slut-shaming joke, but analysis notes she had roughly five confirmed partners vs Raj's at least 10 https://screenrant.com/big-bang-theory-penny-raj-sleep-together/ , undermining conflation of dating jokes with prostitution. The only "prostitute" lines are jokes: e.g. Penny in "The Financial Permeability" asks "That I'm some sort of Chinese food prostitute?" https://the-big-bang-theory.com/quotes/quote/941/ , and season 2 episode "The Vegas Renormalization" features a separate prostitute character Mikayla, not Penny. Darker original unaired pilot female lead Katie (Amanda Walsh) was described as darker/street-hardened and taking advantage of Sheldon/Leonard, but she was scrapped and replaced by Penny https://www.thethings.com/the-big-bang-theory-chuck-lorre-leonard-sheldon-roommate-katie-penny-kaley-cuoco/  — not canon evidence Penny was a prostitute.

## Penny Hofstadter

  
**Penelope "Penny" Hofstadter** is the show _The Big Bang Theory_'s first and always main female protagonist. She lives in [Apartment 4B](/wiki/Apartment_4B "Apartment 4B") with her husband Leonard Hofstadter across the hall from Sheldon Cooper, who lives in apartment 4A where Leonard used to live with Sheldon as roommates. Although the sleeping arrangements are a little complicated. This was an accommodation for Sheldon who was having a very hard time dealing with his break-up with Amy, and Leonard moving out in The 2003 Approximation. Leonard also maintains an office in 4A. Her full first name is possibly "Penelope" as implied by "[The Barbarian Sublimation](/wiki/The_Barbarian_Sublimation "The Barbarian Sublimation")", and her maiden name has never been revealed. But due to her recent marriage to Leonard, her last name is Hofstadter. For a while her last name was Johnson while unknowingly married to ex-boyfriend Zack Johnson. That marriage was annulled in [The Thanksgiving Decoupling](/wiki/The_Thanksgiving_Decoupling "The Thanksgiving Decoupling").

An aspiring, but mostly unsuccessful actress, she was born on a farm near Omaha, Nebraska, and worked at The Cheesecake Factory as a waitress until she quit in "[The Occupation Recalibration](/wiki/The_Occupation_Recalibration "The Occupation Recalibration")" (S7E13) to take up acting full time. Penny is the original female lead in the show before being joined by [Bernadette Rostenkowski](/wiki/Bernadette_Rostenkowski-Wolowitz "Bernadette Rostenkowski-Wolowitz") and [Amy Farrah Fowler](/wiki/Amy_Farrah_Fowler "Amy Farrah Fowler") in seasons 3 and 4, and in season 8, started working at the same company as Bernadette.

Since the pilot, she has always been Leonard's love interest, with the two dating briefly in the first episode of the second season, for most of the third season, and they rekindled their romance in "The Recombination Hypothesis". As of "[The Gorilla Dissolution](/wiki/The_Gorilla_Dissolution "The Gorilla Dissolution")", she and Leonard became engaged and were married at the start of season 9 in The Matrimonial Momentum.

Even though she is considered part of the guys' group, she represents the "dumb blonde" for viewer context in the series with many street smarts and communication skills to compensate for her lack of academic knowledge.

## Physical Appearance\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny is a slender, young woman with fair skin, blond hair and wears different types of clothing, mainly tank tops and jeans.

When she first moved into apartment 4B, she wore a light blue t-shirt, jean short shorts and brown boots.

## Personality\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny is somewhat naive and not thoroughly educated but has a lot of common sense and street smarts. Her dream is to become a famous actress, a goal she never seems to waver from until season 8. She is very kind-hearted and empathetic toward people though she can blow up when made mad, which prompted Leonard to refer to her as The Incredible Hulk" after she went off on Howard. She believes most guys are nice and has been hurt a lot. When someone shocks her, she tends to bat her eyes at them while considering her response. She also walks away when frustrated with people like Sheldon or situations she can't believe or understand. She knows how to throw out wise-cracks and is very loyal to her man as long as she is not betrayed. She also tends to deny doing embarrassing things, or she suddenly realizes they are embarrassing. In the first season, she seemed very naive but has appeared smarter in later seasons and more complicated in situations with her female friends. She also has a habit of being selfish and throwing her friends under the bus. For example, she sold Sheldon out to the court officials for running a red light, despite the fact he had done it to help her after she had dislocated her shoulder, simply because she didn't want the ticket.

### Season 1\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

[![Penny blackmails Sheldon](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/warner-bros-entertainment/images/2/21/Bbt-sheldon-penny.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20220512040537)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/warner-bros-entertainment/images/2/21/Bbt-sheldon-penny.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220512040537)

[](/wiki/File:Bbt-sheldon-penny.jpg)

Penny blackmails Sheldon

In the [first episode](/wiki/Pilot "Pilot") Penny moves into Apartment 4B across from Apartment 4A where Leonard and Sheldon live. She had broken up with her boyfriend Kurt because he cheated on her. She asked the guys for a favor to go get her TV from his apartment, but he steals their pants and Penny apologizes for everything and later the three go out to dinner with Howard and Raj.

In "[The Big Bran Hypothesis](/wiki/The_Big_Bran_Hypothesis "The Big Bran Hypothesis")", Penny asks Leonard and Sheldon to sign for her delivery of her entertainment center. When Sheldon and Leonard, they discover that Penny's apartment is a mess, prompting Sheldon to try to clean it. When Penny arrives, they leave. Unbeknown to her at night, Sheldon cleans up the apartment anyway. When Penny wakes up the next morning, she is infuriated that Sheldon and Leonard came into her apartment while she was asleep, and forces Leonard to give back her spare keys. Sheldon forcefully apologizes to Penny and reveals that he cleaned her apartment. Penny bumps into Raj and she explains the situation, although Raj can't speak to her, he is a good listener, Penny decides to forgive Leonard, and when Leonard tries to apologize, she immediately forgives him.

### Season 2\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D5&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

[![Sheldon helping Penny get an enchanted sword](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/warner-bros-entertainment/images/4/4e/2x03-The-Barbarian-Sublimation-penny-and-sheldon-22774835-1580-888.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20220512040725)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/warner-bros-entertainment/images/4/4e/2x03-The-Barbarian-Sublimation-penny-and-sheldon-22774835-1580-888.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20220512040725)

[](/wiki/File:2x03-The-Barbarian-Sublimation-penny-and-sheldon-22774835-1580-888.jpg)

Sheldon helping Penny get an enchanted sword

After a post-date disagreement, Penny remains friends with all four guys, becomes an integral part of the Social Group and very good friends with Leonard.

In "[The Hofstadter Isotope](/wiki/The_Hofstadter_Isotope "The Hofstadter Isotope")", Penny is asked out on a date by Stuart and things end later in the next episode after it is revealed she called Stuart "Leonard".

In the season finale "[The Monopolar Expedition](/wiki/The_Monopolar_Expedition "The Monopolar Expedition")", Penny wishes Leonard wasn't going to the North Pole and even gives Leonard a blanket as a good luck gift on his expedition to the North Pole.

### Season 3\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D6&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

When the guys return from the North Pole, Penny has missed Leonard enough to express her feelings for him, and they date for most of the season.

Penny introduces her friend Bernadette to Howard as part of a Girlfriend Pact made between Howard and Leonard. Things don't go too smoothly until the two of them find out they both have overbearing mothers.

### Season 4\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D7&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny resumes being part of the guys group and has her own friends, Bernadette, along with Sheldon’s new girlfriend, [Amy](/wiki/Amy_Farrah_Fowler "Amy Farrah Fowler"). Also she realizes that she still has feelings for Leonard, especially since Leonard is dating Priya.

### Season 5\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D8&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Half way through the season (on the 100th episode), Leonard asks Penny out and they reunite, though Penny has misgivings.

### Season 6\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D9&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny works through her doubts and has a stronger relationship with Leonard, as she is now able to say "I love you" to him. They discuss marriage.

### Season 7\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D10&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Penny finds out she is legally married to Zack after Leonard, Sheldon and Amy tell her that weddings in Las Vegas wedding chapels are real when the two thought they were fake. At the end, she and Zack fill out annulment papers and the marriage is legally annulled ("[The Thanksgiving Decoupling](/wiki/The_Thanksgiving_Decoupling "The Thanksgiving Decoupling")"). Penny quits The Cheesecake Factory to concentrate on acting ("[The Occupation Recalibration](/wiki/The_Occupation_Recalibration "The Occupation Recalibration")") and becomes engaged to Leonard after she gets over her clash with the director who fired her ("[The Gorilla Dissolution](/wiki/The_Gorilla_Dissolution "The Gorilla Dissolution")").

### Season 8\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D11&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Between the finale of Season 7 and the premiere of Season 8, Penny drastically changes her look by swapping her usual long blonde locks for a short blonde pixie crop, a look she sports throughout the entire season. She gets a new job at Bernadette's company as a pharmaceutical rep, making excellent progress in her field and spending the year as Leonard's fiancée. At the end of the season, she suggests they head to Vegas to get married.

### Season 9\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D12&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Leonard's little make-out session at sea makes their marriage have a rocky start, but they quickly reconcile though they don't move out of Sheldon's apartment (because of Sheldon going through a bad breakup and due to Sheldon's abandonment issues). At the end of the season, when it's revealed that everyone is upset about not being part of the wedding due to their elopement, Penny suggests having a redo wedding ceremony.

### Season 10\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D13&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

In "The Conjugal Conjecture" Penny and Leonard have their re-wedding ceremony in a park which is officiated by Bernadette.

Penny and Leonard finally have their own apartment, Apartment 4A. In "[The Cohabitation Experimentation](/wiki/The_Cohabitation_Experimentation "The Cohabitation Experimentation")", Amy's apartment suffered water damage, was uninhabitable and she needed a place to stay. Sheldon and Amy started a five week experiment to see if they could manage living together and moved into Penny's old apartment, Apartment 4B. It turned into a permanent arrangement in "[The Veracity Elasticity](/wiki/The_Veracity_Elasticity "The Veracity Elasticity")". Penny also redecorates her and Leonard's bedroom.

### Season 11\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D14&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

While Sheldon proposes to Amy, he gets a call from Leonard and Penny, asking about where he is. He tells them about his unwilling kiss with Ramona and how it made him realize his true feelings about Amy. At the same time, Bernadette tells Penny that she’s pregnant again.

### Season 12\[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPenny_Hofstadter%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D15&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\]

Sheldon and Amy win the Nobel prize with Penny, Leonard, Howard, Bernadette and Raj coming to watch his speech. He then tells the story of his family who has changed his life. Penny And Leonard are soon to be parents.

cascade.findings: Post claims Penny from Big Bang Theory "was a prostitute... implied in the show" and befriended the guys because they were furthest from clients. Canon contradicts this: Penny Hofstadter is established as an aspiring, mostly unsuccessful actress born on a farm near Omaha, Nebraska, who worked at The Cheesecake Factory as a waitress until she quit in "The Occupation Recalibration" (S7E13) to act full-time, later becoming a pharmaceutical rep in season 8 https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Penny_Hofstadter . Pilot canon has her describing her screenplay about a girl from Lincoln, Nebraska who comes to LA to be an actress and ends up a waitress at the cheesecake factory, clarifying "No, I'm from Omaha!" https://the-big-bang-theory.com/quotes/character/Penny/ (pilot quote). No episode, writer or producer source lists sex work as her job; promiscuity is a running slut-shaming joke, but analysis notes she had roughly five confirmed partners vs Raj's at least 10 https://screenrant.com/big-bang-theory-penny-raj-sleep-together/ , undermining conflation of dating jokes with prostitution. The only "prostitute" lines are jokes: e.g. Penny in "The Financial Permeability" asks "That I'm some sort of Chinese food prostitute?" https://the-big-bang-theory.com/quotes/quote/941/ , and season 2 episode "The Vegas Renormalization" features a separate prostitute character Mikayla, not Penny. Darker original unaired pilot female lead Katie (Amanda Walsh) was described as darker/street-hardened and taking advantage of Sheldon/Leonard, but she was scrapped and replaced by Penny https://www.thethings.com/the-big-bang-theory-chuck-lorre-leonard-sheldon-roommate-katie-penny-kaley-cuoco/  — not canon evidence Penny was a prostitute.
